title: The Stain That Needed More Attention
scene: You are about to leave home when you notice a tiny mark on your shirt. A quick attempt to clean it turns into soap, water, a hair dryer, and a completely different shirt.
sceneJa: 家を出る直前、シャツの袖に小さな汚れを見つける。30秒で済ませるつもりの応急処置が、水、石けん、ドライヤーへと広がり、最後は別のシャツに着替えることになる。

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: once I had noticed it / it became surprisingly difficult / to ignore
once I / had noticed it it became / surprisingly difficult to / ignore
once I had / noticed it it / became surprisingly / difficult to ignore
questions.explanation: ‘Once I had noticed it’ sets the condition, ‘it became surprisingly difficult’ gives the result, and ‘to ignore’ completes what became difficult.

questions.question: What does ‘expecting the whole thing to take about thirty seconds’ mean?
options: The speaker thought the cleaning would be quick
The speaker planned to wait thirty seconds before cleaning
The speaker knew the cleaning would take much longer
questions.explanation: The speaker expected a very small task, which makes the later escalation funnier.

questions.question: Why is the final sentence dryly funny?
options: The speaker treats removing the stain as a success even though the attempt made them late
The speaker discovers that the stain was never real
The speaker decides to wear the wet shirt anyway
questions.explanation: The speaker calmly counts the stain as a successful result while ignoring the larger problem created by dealing with it.

speak: Start casually, as if the mark is genuinely minor. Let the frustration build only slightly through the wet patch and soap. Read ‘which mainly improved the size of the problem’ very calmly. Slow down at ‘the stain had almost disappeared, but...’ and deliver the final sentence as a reasonable summary rather than a joke.
review: Today shifts away from recent work, navigation, and train stories into a small domestic problem. The flow is tiny flaw → quick fix → expanding intervention → technically successful outcome. Useful chunks are ‘once I had noticed it’, ‘expecting ... to take ...’, and ‘at least ...’. The humour comes from solving the original problem while creating a more important one.
